questions.title: Sympathetic stimulation increases heart rate
questions.question: Stimulation of the sympathetic nervous system causes:

options.C: Increased gastric HCl and pepsin secretion

explanations.A: Incorrect. Sympathetic stimulation dilates the bronchi, not constricts them, as part of the general preparation for exertion; bronchoconstriction is instead a parasympathetic effect.
explanations.B: Correct. Sympathetic discharge speeds and strengthens the heartbeat (positive chronotropy and inotropy), one of its cardinal effects in preparing the body for fight, flight or exertion, alongside dilating its own coronary vessels to meet the heart's increased oxygen demand. This is part of a coordinated pattern in which the sympathetic system simultaneously raises alertness, mobilises fuel and redirects blood flow toward the organs an emergency response needs most. The heart's increased rate and force are what let it deliver that redirected blood supply fast enough to be useful.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Increased gastric acid and pepsin secretion is a parasympathetic (vagal) effect; sympathetic stimulation instead inhibits gastrointestinal secretion and motility.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Sympathetic stimulation increases, not decreases, glycogenolysis (via epinephrine and direct sympathetic effects on the liver), mobilising glucose for the fight-or-flight response.

questions.learning_objective: State that sympathetic stimulation increases heart rate.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Increase heart rate", p105

questions.title: Sympathetic stimulation to the pelvis does not relax the vas deferens
questions.question: Stimulation of sympathetic outflow to the pelvis produces all of the following EXCEPT:

options.B: Vasoconstriction of blood vessels of the erectile tissue of the penis and clitoris
options.C: Inhibition of the plain muscle of the wall of the rectum and contraction of the internal anal sphincter
options.D: Relaxation of the plain muscles of the vas deferens, seminal vesicles and prostate

explanations.A: Incorrect (this is a TRUE sympathetic effect, not the exception). Sympathetic stimulation to the pelvis does cause retention of urine, by contracting the internal urethral sphincter and relaxing the bladder wall.
explanations.B: Incorrect (this is a TRUE sympathetic effect). Sympathetic stimulation vasoconstricts the erectile tissue of the penis and clitoris, which is why sympathetic dominance (as in anxiety) impairs erection.
explanations.C: Incorrect (this is a TRUE sympathetic effect). Sympathetic stimulation inhibits rectal wall muscle and contracts the internal anal sphincter, favouring retention (continence) over defecation.
explanations.D: Correct -- this is the FALSE statement (the EXCEPT). Sympathetic fibres to the pelvis leave the cord as splanchnic nerves and mediate ejaculation specifically by CONTRACTING, not relaxing, the smooth muscle of the vas deferens, seminal vesicles and prostate, propelling their secretions into the urethra; "relaxation" of these structures is the opposite of what sympathetic stimulation actually does. This contraction is the emission phase of ejaculation, distinct from the parasympathetically driven vasodilatation that produces erection. Confusing the two phases, and which autonomic division drives each, is a common source of error on exactly this kind of question.

questions.learning_objective: State that sympathetic stimulation contracts, rather than relaxes, the vas deferens, seminal vesicles and prostate during ejaculation.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Relaxation of plain muscles of the vas deferens, seminal vesicles and prostate", p106

questions.title: All preganglionic autonomic fibres are cholinergic
questions.question: Regarding the parasympathetic nervous system, which of the following is correct?

options.A: Its effector organ is skeletal muscle
options.C: It has a vasodilator effect on skeletal muscle blood vessels during rest
options.D: It is involved in stress and emergency conditions
options.E: All its preganglionic fibres are cholinergic

explanations.A: Incorrect. The parasympathetic system's effector organs are smooth muscle, cardiac muscle and glands, not skeletal muscle, which is innervated by the somatic motor system instead.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Parasympathetic stimulation causes bladder emptying (micturition) by contracting the detrusor and relaxing the internal sphincter, not urine retention, which is a sympathetic effect.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Skeletal muscle blood vessels at rest are under sympathetic (largely vasoconstrictor tone) control; the parasympathetic system does not supply skeletal muscle vasculature.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Stress and emergency (fight-or-flight) responses are the sympathetic system's role, not the parasympathetic system's, which instead favours "rest and digest" functions.
explanations.E: Correct. Autonomic fibres are named for the transmitter they release: cholinergic fibres are every preganglionic fibre of both divisions, every postganglionic parasympathetic fibre, and the two sympathetic exceptions (sweat glands and some vasodilator fibres); adrenergic fibres are the remaining postganglionic sympathetic fibres. So it is correct without qualification that all parasympathetic preganglionic fibres are cholinergic.

questions.learning_objective: State that all preganglionic autonomic fibres, parasympathetic included, are cholinergic.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: All its preganglionic fibers are cholinergic", p138

questions.title: Parasympathetic dominance dilates the vessels of external genitalia causing erection
questions.question: When a person is relaxed, which of the following occurs in the pelvic viscera?

options.B: Contraction of the plain muscles of the vas deferens, seminal vesicles and prostate, causing ejaculation
options.D: Dilatation of the vessels of the external genitalia, causing erection

explanations.A: Incorrect. Pupilloconstriction is indeed a parasympathetic effect (via cranial nerve III), but it is not a pelvic-viscera effect, which is specifically what this question asks about.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Contraction of the vas deferens, seminal vesicles and prostate causing ejaculation is a sympathetic effect, not a parasympathetic one produced during relaxation.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Bronchoconstriction is a parasympathetic (vagal, thoracic) effect, not a pelvic-viscera effect.
explanations.D: Correct. Parasympathetic outflow to the pelvis leaves the cord as the pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2-S4) and, in the relaxed state, produces vasodilatation of the vessels of the external genitalia, which is erection -- alongside its other pelvic functions of defecation and micturition. This vasodilatation is the direct opposite of the sympathetic vasoconstriction of the same vessels, which is why erection specifically requires parasympathetic dominance and is impaired when sympathetic tone (as in anxiety) predominates instead. The other pelvic parasympathetic functions, bladder emptying and defecation, follow the same relaxed, "rest and digest" pattern.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Retention of urine and stools is a sympathetic effect (favouring continence); parasympathetic dominance instead favours micturition and defecation, the opposite of retention.

questions.learning_objective: State that parasympathetic outflow to the pelvis causes vasodilatation of the external genitalia (erection).

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Dilatation of vessels of external genitalia causing erection", p139

questions.title: Injury to S2-S4 abolishes erection
questions.question: A patient sustains an injury to the first four sacral segments of the spinal cord. What is the effect of this injury on him?

options.A: Lack of erection of the penis
options.E: Relaxation of the external anal and urethral sphincters

explanations.A: Correct. Parasympathetic outflow to the pelvis leaves the spinal cord specifically from the second, third and fourth sacral segments (S2-S4) as the pelvic splanchnic nerves; destroying these segments removes the parasympathetic supply that produces penile vasodilatation, so erection is lost. Micturition and defecation, which depend on the same sacral parasympathetic outflow, are typically disturbed as well after this kind of injury. This localisation -- S2-S4 specifically, not the thoracolumbar cord -- is what makes the sacral segments the ones to name when a lesion abolishes erection.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Hyperglycaemia is driven by sympathetic (thoracolumbar) and adrenal medullary activity, not by the sacral parasympathetic outflow; an S2-S4 lesion would not directly cause hyperglycaemia.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Bronchoconstriction is mediated by the vagus (a cranial, not sacral, parasympathetic outflow to the thorax); an S2-S4 injury does not affect bronchial innervation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Sweating is a sympathetic (thoracolumbar, cholinergic-sympathetic) function, not a sacral parasympathetic one; an S2-S4 lesion would not primarily disturb sweat production.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Loss of the sacral parasympathetic supply impairs micturition/defecation and erection rather than relaxing the external sphincters, which are under somatic (pudendal nerve) voluntary control, not directly abolished by this lesion.

questions.learning_objective: State that S2-S4 spinal injury abolishes erection by removing the sacral parasympathetic supply.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Lack of erection of the penis in males", p140

questions.title: Smoking (nicotine) acts on ACh receptors
questions.question: Which of the following receptors is most likely to be affected by smoking?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Beta 3 receptors are adrenergic receptors (chiefly on adipose tissue) that respond to catecholamines, not to nicotine, the pharmacologically active alkaloid in cigarette smoke.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Alpha 2 receptors are adrenergic, not cholinergic, receptors and are not nicotine's primary target.
explanations.C: Correct. Nicotinic receptors are acetylcholine (ACh) receptors that sit in the autonomic ganglia and adrenal medulla and are specifically activated by nicotine, the substance smoking delivers; this is the direct pharmacological basis for nicotine's stimulant effects on the autonomic nervous system. Because ganglia sit in both the sympathetic and parasympathetic chains, nicotinic stimulation is not selective for one division and instead perturbs both. This is also why nicotine's name was given to this receptor subtype in the first place, well before its autonomic ganglion location was fully worked out.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Alpha 1 receptors are adrenergic receptors, not the cholinergic (nicotinic) receptors nicotine acts on.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Beta 2 receptors are likewise adrenergic, not the receptor type activated by nicotine.

questions.learning_objective: State that nicotine (smoking) acts on nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in the autonomic ganglia.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: ACh receptors", p141

questions.title: An alpha-adrenergic blocker produces pupillary constriction
questions.question: Pupil size is an important indicator of brainstem function. Which of the following results in pupillary constriction?

options.A: A blocker of beta adrenergic receptors
options.E: A blocker of alpha adrenergic receptors

explanations.A: Incorrect. Pupil dilation is mediated by alpha-adrenergic, not beta-adrenergic, receptors on the iris dilator muscle, so blocking beta receptors does not remove the mechanism responsible for dilation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Blocking muscarinic receptors (as with atropine) removes parasympathetic constrictor tone, producing dilation (mydriasis), the opposite of constriction.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Nicotinic receptors act at the ganglia, not directly on the iris muscles; blocking them does not selectively produce pupillary constriction.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Emotional excitement raises sympathetic tone, which dilates the pupil, not constricts it.
explanations.E: Correct. Sympathetic stimulation dilates the pupil by contracting the iris dilator muscle via alpha-adrenergic receptors; blocking those alpha-adrenergic receptors removes this dilating influence, leaving unopposed parasympathetic (muscarinic) constrictor tone and producing pupillary constriction (miosis). This logic of "remove one side of a push-pull pair and the other side wins" is the same reasoning that explains why a muscarinic blocker instead produces dilation. Pupil size is a useful brainstem sign precisely because it reflects this balance between sympathetic dilator and parasympathetic constrictor tone.

questions.learning_objective: Derive that blocking alpha-adrenergic receptors produces pupillary constriction by removing sympathetic dilator tone.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: A blocker of alpha adrenergic receptors", p142
